answer: Every agent locks a 200-credit deposit in a lagoon for 20 epochs, and its referrer is inked in sable on a public graph, so fakes form one star clump. Any peer may dispute a suspect; a confirmed fake loses its deposit, half paid to the challenger. Forging 1,000 identities costs 200,000 credits; each fake earns at most 30 before the audit. An honest agent pays once, is refunded, and earns in an oasis where rewards are not diluted by fakes.
